event: Rain-triggered landslide at Simaltal, Bharatpur-29, sweeps two buses (Ganapati Deluxe, Kathmandu to Gaur; Angel Deluxe, Birgunj to Kathmandu) off the Narayangadh-Muglin road into the swollen Trishuli. 65 people aboard.
Three passengers jump from a bus and swim to the banks; locals find them and take them to hospital.
14 bodies recovered, some washed up to 100 km downstream. 8 identified, including 6 Indian nationals. First identified body: Rishi Pal Shahi, 40.
source: PA News 16 Jul 2024; PTI via Latestly

event: Bodies of Ganapati Deluxe driver Kishor Kumar Chaudhary, 35, and conductor Rishi Kumar Singh, 48, recovered near the Gandak Barrage, 103 km downstream.
A 12-member Indian NDRF team joins the search. (Exact arrival date not reported; placed mid-July.)
25 bodies found; one later ruled unrelated to the crash. 7 remain unidentified; of the identified, 16 male and 2 female, 13 Nepali and 5 Indian.

Suspected wreckage of the Ganapati bus found buried in sand near Dwandrang Bensi, Aanbukhaireni-5, Tanahun; police say full recovery needed for confirmation. Radio Nepal: 65 aboard, 11 bodies recovered, 3 survivors, 51 missing.
